storeListing.shortDescription: Offline blood sugar logbook. Free. No account. Data stays on your phone.
storeListing.fullDescription:
SugarTrack is a simple Android logbook for blood sugar. Free. No account. No internet. Everything stays on the phone.

Log a reading with the time, context (fasting, before or after a meal, bedtime, or random), an optional note, and an optional photo of the meal. See the latest value on the home screen against the target range you set. Browse history and a trend graph. Log medications and A1C results. Set a daily reminder. Export a PDF or CSV to take to a doctor visit.

Units can be mg/dL or mmol/L.

SugarTrack is a logbook, not a glucose meter and not medical advice. Readings come from your own meter. Talk to a doctor about what the numbers mean.

Health numbers are personal. SugarTrack does not talk to a server, does not require a login, and does not send readings anywhere.

appAccess.notes: No accounts. The app works offline after install.

contentRatings.notes: Complete the IARC questionnaire in Console; expect Everyone / PEGI 3 style rating.

dataSafety.notes: On-device only. Google still counts user-entered health logs and optional photos as collected data even when they never leave the phone.

dataTypes.type: Health info (blood sugar logs, medications, A1C)

securityPractices.notes: No network transfer of user data. Users can export files themselves via the share sheet.

dataSafety.deletionHow: Delete readings in the app, clear app storage, or uninstall.

health.description: Personal logbook. User types values from their own meter. Not a medical device and not medical advice.

photosAndVideosPermission.userFacingReason: Optional photos of meals attached to a reading. The app does not record audio. Microphone permission may appear because of the camera library; it is not used.

closedTesting.track: Closed testing (Play Console). EAS submit track value: alpha
steps: Create a closed testing email list (see testers.csv).
Upload the production AAB to Closed testing (manual or eas submit --profile production).
Copy the opt-in URL and send it to testers.
Testers must open the link, opt in, and install from Play — adding an email is not enough.
Keep the release live for 14 days, then apply for production access and send production for review.
